newsitem.title: USA: Warm weather aids Iowa corn, soybeans and weeds.
newsitem.headline: Warm weather aids Iowa corn, soybeans and weeds.

text.p: Warm weather during the week ended Sunday aided Iowa corn and soybeans, as well as weeds which required spraying by farmers, according to the state's weekly Agricultural Statistics Service report.

Although higher than previous weeks, temperatures still averaged below normal throughout southeast Iowa. The hay crop was in the worst shape of the major crops, with low yields and decreased quality reported in early alfalfa cuttings.

Corn emergence was at 98 percent versus 91 a year ago and the 86 average. About two percent of the acreage will have to be replanted versus four a year ago. Recent cool weather also had slowed development.
Corn improved slightly from a week ago to 13 percent excellent, 59 good, 26 fair, and two poor.

Soybeans were 99 percent planted versus 71 last year and the 78 percent average, while emergence was 86 percent versus 43 last year and the 57 average. Crusting in southwest fields slowed emergence there.
Oats improved slightly with the crop rated 65 percent good to excellent, 31 percent fair and four percent poor.
Winter wheat was rated 61 percent good to excellent, 35 fair and four percent poor.

The first alfalfa cutting was 17 percent harvested, five days ahead of last year and three days ahead of the average. The condition decreased from a week ago to four percent excellent, 33 good, 43 fair, 16 poor and four very poor.
Pastures improved to five percent excellent, 43 good, 41 fair, nine poor, and two very poor.
Topsoil moisture was rated three percent surplus, 78 adequate and 19 short.
